uplink.description: Switch frame (opcode 6): state byte 5 -> switch0 + switch2 closed, switch1 open; 3.6 V
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds Mutelcor switch frame. State byte 0x05 sets bits 0x01 and 0x04, so the zero-based entries switch0 and switch2 are closed and switch1 is open. Same input and same per-bit convention as the pre-channels vector; the old `switch1`/`switch2`/`switch3` extras and the old top-level action.contactState (bit 0) are now the three entries. Voltage bytes[1..2] = 0x0168 = 360 centivolts -> battery 3.6 V (whole-device, stays top-level).

uplink.description: Switch frame (opcode 6): mixed pattern, state byte 2 -> only switch1 closed while the primary switch0 is open
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds multi-position frame: state byte 0x02 sets only bit 0x02. This is the case that pins the renumbering — the primary switch (bit 0, which used to be BOTH the top-level action.contactState and `switch1`) reads open while the second input reads closed, so an off-by-one in the label mapping would flip both entries and fail the vector.

uplink.description: Switch frame (opcode 6): state 0 -> all three switches open
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds switch frame with no bit set. All three entries are still emitted: the state byte carries no presence mask, so an unwired input is indistinguishable from an open contact and no entry is suppressed (see the codec header's sentinel policy).

uplink.description: Measurements frame (opcode 3) carries no contact state
uplink._note: Synthetic. Non-switch opcodes carry no dry-contact input, so no measurement (and no `channels` key) is produced; the error string is unchanged from the pre-channels codec.

uplink.description: Switch frame (opcode 6) truncated before the state byte
uplink._note: Synthetic. Guards the sentinel policy: without bytes[4] the codec errors rather than reading `undefined` and fabricating three open contacts.
